title: Stack Snapshot Trace Builder
prompt:
A sampling profiler periodically records the active call stack. Convert its samples into a trace showing when calls begin and end.

Implement `stack_samples_to_trace_events(samples, min_samples=1) -> list[dict]`. Each sample is `(timestamp, stack)`, with frame names ordered from the outermost call to the innermost. Samples arrive in nondecreasing timestamp order.

Return events of the form `{'name': frame, 'phase': 'B' or 'E', 'timestamp': timestamp}`. A call begins when it first appears and ends at the first sample where it is absent. At the same timestamp, end inner calls before their parents, then begin parent calls before their children. A call is identified by its complete path from the outermost frame: the same name under a different parent, or at a different recursive depth, is a different call. Calls still present in the final sample remain open.

Follow-up: suppress calls observed in fewer than `min_samples` consecutive samples. In this version, emit a begin event at the timestamp of the confirming sample, and an end event only for a previously confirmed call. With `min_samples=1`, this is the base behavior. Returning after an absence starts a new streak.

Accept an iterable of samples without requiring the full input history in memory. Empty input returns `[]`. Assume finite numeric timestamps and nonempty string frame names; do not mutate the input. `min_samples` must be a positive integer.

example.reasoning: The load call has ended by the second sample. The main and parse calls have no observed end.

references.label: Notion interview record; event schema and confirming-sample timestamps are practice conventions
Public prompt summary (secondary): open final calls and consecutive-sample follow-up
